messages:
PagerDuty Bot: P1 alert fired for service=api-public - high error rate and TLS handshakes failing. Incident INC-210124 created. Paging on-call.

Network Bot: Automated health checks flagged elevated 502/524 and TLS handshake failures originating from Cloudflare POPs in EU and APAC.

Maya Patel: I'm seeing client TLS errors and increased 5xx from frontdoors starting ~07:40 UTC. Synthetic checks: ~22% error rate, spikes coincide with CF edge errors. Adding thread here.

Samir Khan: logs show patterns of SNI mismatch and "tls: unknown_cert" on several upstream connections. Example:
```
2026-03-15T07:41:02Z error: http2: server sent GOAWAY: err_code=0x1 description="tls: unexpected certificate"
cf-edge: edge-eu-2
```

Irene Lee: confirmed impacted regions via Datadog: EU-West and APAC-Tokyo spikes. Support queue has an influx of 408/502 tickets. Initial customer impact estimate: 20-40% for EU traffic, intermittent for APAC.

Alex Gomez: CF status shows "partial degradation for TLS termination" in affected POPs. Opening CF support ticket now (CF-9999) and requesting per-edge SNI/TLS debug logs.

Maya Patel: mitigation options: 1) rotate to direct origin DNS (disable proxy) for critical endpoints; 2) add short-lived CNAME to failover ALB in us-west for major customers; 3) reduce app timeouts to prevent cascading origin overload if retries spike.

Samir Khan: validating origin health before flip: direct curl OK (TLS handshakes succeed, 200). We'll prefer DNS bypass but need to coordinate firewall updates and cert exposure.

Irene Lee: can we temporarily restrict origin ingress to Cloudflare IP blocks only while we keep proxy? If we disable proxy, we must open to new IPs or use signed URLs. I'll coordinate with infra.

Maya Patel: doing a controlled grey-cloud off for write endpoints on api.redwood.ai for a subset (canary customers) to measure impact. Not doing global yet.

Network Bot: change logged: grey-cloud disabled for write-route canary set at 07:46 UTC.

Samir Khan: after canary flip errors dropped for those customers to <2%. Global error rate dropped from 22% to 8%.

Alex Gomez: CF replied: they pushed an edge rule update that mismatched SNI routing for a small percentage of routes in EU/APAC due to a config race during rollout. They're rolling back changesets and will provide timeline. ETA ~20m.

Irene Lee: preparing DNS fallback plan. Creating Route53 change batch to add failover ALB with TTL 20s and health checks. Also drafting comms to CS about temporary workaround: use region-specific endpoint (us-west) for critical workflows.

Maya Patel: note on security: disabling Cloudflare proxy leaks origin IPs. Samir, please ensure origin security group restricted to CF IP list if we re-enable proxy, and rotate certs if we go public.

Samir Khan: taking action: pre-warming ALB target groups and adding strict rate limiting on origin to protect from retry storms. Also enabling short-circuit cache for static endpoints.

Network Bot: Route53 change submitted (change id C210124-1) to add failover ALB with TTL=20s at 07:53 UTC.

Alex Gomez: CF update: rollback in progress in EU/ASIA POPs, edge config rollback completed in EU-WEST, APAC rollback ~60% done. They flagged root cause: inconsistency in SNI table after parallel deployments. They will provide edge logs and postmortem link soon.

Irene Lee: monitoring shows further improvement as rollbacks proceed. Global 5xx now ~3%, EU ~1.2% at 08:00 UTC. Keeping DNS TTL low for 30m to allow faster failover if needed.

Maya Patel: drafting public status: "We are investigating degraded API reachability due to a third-party CDN provider affecting TLS termination in select regions. We have applied temporary routing changes and partial bypass for critical customers. We will update every 30 minutes. INC-210124." Sending to Comms for review.

Samir Khan: note for follow-up: gather Cloudflare edge logs, collect SNI mismatch traces, audit recent CF config pushes, and prepare to rotate certs if origin IPs were exposed.

Alex Gomez: posted CF ticket link and assigned CF engineer to send SNI and TLS traces. CF case: https://support.cloudflare.com/cases/CF-9999

Irene Lee: handoff plan: @Maya Patel -> @Irene Lee at 08:05 UTC. I will keep monitoring and coordinate post-incident review. Keep grey-cloud off for now until CF confirms stable.

PagerDuty Bot: Handoff reminder sent to @Irene Lee. No further pages until escalation.

Irene Lee: marking mitigations successful at 08:13 UTC. Final metrics: global 5xx <1%, EU transient ~0.8%. Closing operational thread; will open postmortem doc with timeline and action items. :white_check_mark:
_meta: synthetic incident thread for incidents channel
